newsitem.title: USA: Stocks drift higher on buying of blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Stocks drift higher on buying of blue chips.

text.p: Stocks drifted higher in quiet trading Monday as a small group of blue-chip stocks continued to lead the market higher.

"The same stocks continue to go up," said Scott Bleier, chief investmemt strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "People are chasing yields and buying defensive, yield-oriented stocks like telecoms and oils."

Just after 1 p.m., the Dow Jones industrial average added 19.22 points to 6,580.13, extending its run into record territory. The 30-share Dow rose 14.23 points on Friday to close at a record 6,560.91.
The Dow was led by gains in its three oil components: Texaco added 1-1/4 to 100; Chevron gained 1 to 67 and Exxon rose 3/4 to 100-5/8.
AT&T, another Dow component, also extended its recent rally, adding 1/2 to 44-1/4.

Beyond the solid gains tallied by a few blue-chip issues, the session was extremely quiet, with volume a light 150 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange just after midday. Advancing issues led decliners by about five to four.
With most year-end tax-related selling probably over, analysts said the recent upswing in the market could spread to secondary stocks, but for now the buying interest remained narrowly focused.

"One would expect the laggards to pick up now that tax-loss selling is wrapping up," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co. "But generally speaking, buyers are very selective right now."
Technology shares were a mixed bag at midday, although one very slender segment of the technology sector rallied sharply.

Computer service companies that specialise in developing software to deal with the so-called "Year 2000" problem jumped as investors continued to show a ferocious appetite for the stocks. Older computer software, mostly designed for mainframes, will not recognise "00" in a two-digit year entry as 2000 but as 1900, meaning the software needs to be fixed.

One of the companies, Zitel Corp. surged 7-5/8 to 68-7/8. Zitel shares have tripled in value since the start of December. Others included Acceler8 Technology, up 6-5/8 to 28-1/8 and TSR Inc., up 8 to 45-1/2.
Some analysts said interest in the stocks was intense but that the issues seemed to be getting ahead of themselves.
The Standard & Poor's 500 index added 1.20 points to 757.99.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.16 point to 1,291.54.
The American Stock Exchange index added 1.29 to 583.22.
